title: Terraform module: GPU autoscale nodegroup for Private VPC with robust health probes and upgrade lifecycle
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a reusable Terraform module to provision GPU node groups in Private (VPC) deployments that supports both ASG-based and Karpenter-based autoscaling modes, includes platform-level health probes, and provides safe rolling upgrades for node image/kernel and driver updates.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes variables to switch autoscaler mode: 'autoscaler_mode' with values 'asg'|'karpenter'
Module provisions node group with configurable GPU instance types, taints, labels, and IAM role bindings suitable for Private deployments
Health checks: node-level systemd probe + kubelet readiness integration + optional Prometheus/CloudWatch exporter configuration
Upgrade workflow: instance refresh + lifecycle hooks for ASG and equivalent graceful replacement for Karpenter; automated pod eviction and KV cache warming hooks
Lifecycle policies ensure no loss of in-flight inference traffic beyond config SLO (configurable maxUnavailable/parallelDrain)
Module outputs clear resource names and tags for integration with console telemetry and billing (node pool id, autoscaler type, launch template id)
E2E test playbook validates scaling up/down, node failure handling, and rolling upgrade without user-visible 503s for a baseline load
implementation_notes: Design pattern: single module supports two backends (ASG/Karpenter). Internally create mutually exclusive resources via count/for_each guarded by 'autoscaler_mode' variable

ASG path: create launch template with GPU driver bootstrap script, SSM parameter for driver version, autoscaling group with lifecycle hooks to call a Lambda for pre-terminate drain and KV cache presign warming
Karpenter path: generate provisioner CR manifest via templatefile and apply via k8s provider. Ensure nodeSelector/taints and required labels are injected from module outputs
Health checks: combine instance-level 'ec2-instance-status' with a custom systemd timer that reports to CloudWatch. Add optional daemonset 'node-health-exporter' that emits a 'gpu_driver_ok' metric

Upgrade safety: implement 'drain_before_terminate' logic using AWS lifecycle hooks for ASG; for Karpenter rely on node deletion with pre-drain using 'kubectl drain' executed via a privileged job in the control cluster

Terraform ergonomics: expose variables for spot vs reserved (spot_capacity), max_unavailable, min_ready_seconds, kubelet_extra_args, and driver_version. Provide sensible defaults for private deployments.
IAM: module must create least-privilege IAM role for nodes, allow SSM:GetParameter, CloudWatch put-metric, ECR pull, and S3 read for model caches when enabled
Outputs: node_pool_name, autoscaler_mode, launch_template_id (asg path), provisioner_name (karpenter path), instance_profile_arn
tests: Unit: terraform plan diffs for both modes using mock variables (tfsec + checkov static scans)
Integration: deploy into a staging VPC, run workload that pins a small inference service to GPUs, verify scaledown preserves cache hits across warmers
Chaos: simulate mid-request node termination and verify graceful handoff and no more than 1% request error increase under baseline load
Upgrade: perform a driver_version bump and verify rolling replace honors max_unavailable and succeeds without manual intervention
rollout_plan: Step 1: Merge module into internal registry and publish 0.1.0 to terraform module registry
Step 2: Add module to one non-critical PRD-like private customer environment (canary) and monitor health for 72h
Step 3: Run coordinated upgrade job for in-place driver updates across other private clusters during off-peak windows
Step 4: Enable Karpenter path for one cluster and monitor node provisioning latency and pod startup telemetry
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: spot/interruptible instances can cause elevated eviction; Mitigation: expose spot_capacity and prefer mixed-instances with fallback reserved pool
Risk: Kubernetes drain might extend beyond SLO if workloads pin GPUs for long-running jobs; Mitigation: support preDrain hooks to checkpoint or requeue jobs and configurable maxDrainTimeout

Risk: driver/kernel mismatches during upgrades; Mitigation: use SSM parameterized driver_version and preflight checks in bootstrap script that report failure to CloudWatch and prevent instance from joining the ASG/Karpenter pool
Risk: Terraform drift if cluster resources are changed via kubectl; Mitigation: document which resources are managed and publish a reconciliation job in the ops repo
